narr: Isolated thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours on the 12th in the Quad State. Wind damage occurred in the town of Sesser, including tree and powerline damage. Storms from the previous evening in Sesser might have made some trees more susceptible to damage. Meanwhile, torrential rainfall with nearly stationary storms near Tamaroa produced flash flooding. Isolated storms continued overnight as heavy rain and minimal storm motion caused flash flooding issues in Murphysboro and other locations in or near Jackson County, Illinois. Storm total rainfall peaked around 2-3 inches in parts of Jackson and Perry Counties, most of which fell within an hour or two at each respective location. Shear was minimal while SBCAPE reached 2000-3000 J/kg during the afternoon on the 12th, dropping to 1000-2000 J/kg overnight. PW values were near 1.75 inch.
ev: A water rescue occurred at the Union Pacific Railroad underpass on Business Hwy 13 with water halfway up the door. Another vehicle was stalled in high water at 14th and Maple Streets in Murphysboro. Water came into the door of a residence in the 1200 block of N 14th St. Radar estimated 3-hr rainfall totals were 2-3.5 inches most of which fell between 215-330CST.

Roads in northeast Jackson County were flooded by heavy rains. Field flooding lingered with drainage ditches swollen and flowing. Radar estimated 3-hour rainfall totals were 2 to 4 inches with the highest amounts falling just northeast of Vergennes between 300-500CST.
Street flooding occurred in Cobden. 1.45 inches of rain fell between 315-350CST.

Road flooding was reported in northeastern portions of Perry County, including US-51 north of Tamaroa. Radar estimated rainfall totals between 1445-1615CST were around 3 inches just north of Tamaroa and 1.5-2 inches in Tamaroa.
